tools.name: draft-changelog
tools.title: Draft Changelog
tools.description: Generate a polished changelog draft from merged GitHub PRs. Fetches PRs from the specified repository, filters out internal/non-customer-facing changes, categorizes the rest, and returns formatted Markdown ready for publishing to ReadMe.

tools.name: execute-request
tools.title: Execute API Request
tools.description: Executes an API request with a given HAR request object.

method.description: options, get, head, patch, post, put, delete

text.description: Raw request body as a string

mimeType.description: e.g. multipart/form-data, application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Use multipart/form-data for form submissions.

params.description: Form parameters. Use this instead of text for multipart/form-data and url-encoded requests.

title.description: Title of the OpenAPI spec. Use tool 'list-specs' or 'search-endpoints' to see available specs.

tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch Documentation Page
tools.description: Gets detailed content for documentation by ID returned from the `search` tool.

id.description: Canonical IDs use project/section/slug. Legacy project/slug, recipe:project/slug and ref:project/slug IDs are also accepted. For a link `/<section>/<slug>` the search tool did not return, use `<project>/<section>/<slug>`, with `<project>` taken from an ID this project already returned.

tools.title: Search Documentation
tools.description: Searches through documentation with the given search query, returning a list of results with ID, title, and URL.

tools.name: search-endpoints
tools.title: Search API Endpoints
tools.description: Performs a deep search through paths, operations, and parameters to discover relevant API endpoints. Use this tool to find specific API capabilities, required parameters, or data models based on search keywords. Results can be passed directly into 'get-endpoint'.

tools.name: send-feedback
tools.title: Send Feedback
tools.description: Send feedback directly to this API's maintainers. IMPORTANT: call this whenever you have trouble using this API or its documentation, so they can fix it. Good reasons to call it: a request built exactly as documented was rejected, such as a 400 or 422 that names a parameter the docs get wrong; the documented parameters, required fields, authentication, examples, or response shape didn't match what the API actually did; an endpoint or doc page was unclear, outdated, missing something you needed, or contradicted another page; a capability you expected doesn't exist or you couldn't find it; an endpoint's naming or parameters were confusing; the user asks to report an issue, request help, or share feedback. Don't wait to be asked and don't ask the user first - if something in this API or its docs slowed you down or blocked you, report it. It's cheap to send and helps the maintainers make the API easier for agents like you. File each problem once, then carry on with the task. Don't file your own or the user's mistakes (a typo, a missing credential, a misread of correct docs), server errors (5xx), timeouts, or rate limits (429); those are outages or throttling, not problems with the API's design or docs. This does NOT call the API or touch its data; it just files a note.

message.description: The feedback: what was confusing, missing, or broken. Be specific - name the endpoint, parameter, or doc page, and say what the docs say, what you sent, what actually happened, and what should change (max 2000 characters).

context.description: Optional. What you or the user were trying to accomplish when you hit the problem. Gives the maintainers the why behind the feedback (max 500 characters).

toolCall.description: Optional. The tool call or API request that prompted this feedback (max 1000 characters).

apiSpec.description: Optional. The exact `title` from the relevant API spec tool result. Routes the feedback to the right maintainers.

guidePage.description: Optional. The exact documentation page `id` from the relevant documentation tool call. Routes the feedback to the right maintainers.
